purpose covered: Purpose (class header: helpers for pushing node declarations from deployment user directories; script header: push changes as if they came from your account) is read correctly. The checks run commush.sh as behaviour in a real clone against a local bare origin: install (owner/mode/bytes), a confirmed run with no branch argument (default master) committing only tracked changes as the given name/email with the typed message and pushing to origin master while the untracked file stays untracked and out of origin, a declined run changing nothing, a missing email giving usage and rc 1, and the non-stopping branch-mismatch warning on another branch. The round-1 gaps (default branch, untracked exclusion) are now exercised. The one uncovered row (https remote and token prompt, lines 6 and 39) is honest: the script's git commands are remote-agnostic and the authentication is git's and the server's; only the static token echo is untested, which is not part of the class's job. Its lifted_by names the default ubuntu kind (an https git server would be needed there), which is loose but not a misstatement of what the checks leave out.
